confidence.arithmetic: Exact decimal accounting, checked input contracts and matching observation dates.
confidence.economic: Descriptive proxy with incomplete balance-sheet coverage; no causal or predictive confidence claim.
confidence.temporal: Current-vintage monitoring. Archive-known availability only, beginning with saved captures; no historical PIT backtest.

omitted: Captured source HTML and site assets
Private capture directory and original full manifest
evidence_scope.verification: Published numerical input hashes, declared contracts, calculations, CSV and HTML output. Original source-page metadata checks cannot be repeated because those webpages are omitted. Neither signed source authenticity nor historical release/revision times are verified.

interpretation: The latest complete Wednesday is 2026-10-14. Over four calendar weeks the selected liquidity proxy rose by 111.980 USD bn. Treasury general account had the largest absolute accounting contribution (105.885 USD bn). Observed reserves changed by 109.318 USD bn, while the proxy–reserve gap changed by 2.662 USD bn. These movements describe selected balance-sheet positions; they do not identify a policy shock or establish an asset-price forecast.

methodology.alignment: Exact Wednesday dates; no resampling, interpolation, or filling
methodology.interpretation: Recipe 1 decomposes selected balance-sheet positions; recipe 2 compares them with observed reserves and measures the residual gap. These are accounting descriptions, not causal estimates or trading signals.
limitations: US Federal Reserve balance sheet only; not global liquidity, broad money, private credit, or tradable cash.
Total reverse repos include foreign official and international accounts and other reverse repos. This is not the popular assets-minus-TGA-minus-ON-RRP formula.
The gap includes omitted liabilities and capital; it is not an unexplained statistical error or a complete reconciliation of every H.4.1 line.
Current-vintage history is unsuitable for a historical point-in-time backtest. Observation dates do not establish publication or availability dates.
Per-observation historical publication dates and vintages are not retrieved. Snapshot comparisons establish changes seen between captures, not the time or reason an official revision occurred.
The 10-calendar-day stale threshold is an operational warning, not a release-calendar forecast. Same-day captures can straddle an upstream update.
A rising proxy does not establish easier financial conditions or predictive market returns. No live trading or investment recommendation.
